title: Erdős 257 Mersenne digit terms: summability under every binary selector

concepts.label: Binary Mersenne digit term
concepts.description: At coordinate k, mersenneDigitTerm k b is the binary digit b(k), viewed in the reals, multiplied by the positive Mersenne weight 1/(2^(k+1)-1).

concepts.label: Summable Mersenne-weight majorant
concepts.description: Each binary digit term has norm at most its corresponding Mersenne weight, and the full positive-index Mersenne-weight series is summable.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every binary selector b : Nat -> Fin 2, the real series with kth term mersenneDigitTerm k b = b(k) * mersenneWeight (k+1) is summable. The proof is uniform in b: each digit is 0 or 1, so the term norm is bounded by mersenneWeight (k+1), whose series is already summable.
statement_nodes.engine: Norm domination by summable_mersenneWeight via norm_mersenneDigitTerm_le and Summable.of_norm_bounded.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A direct dominated-series consequence of summability of the Mersenne weights and the 0/1 digit bound; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This theorem establishes analytic summability only. It does not compute the sum, prove uniqueness or injectivity of the digit coding, state the one-coordinate update formula, classify an achievement set or its measure, constrain the selected support, or settle any irrationality assertion in Problem 257.

declaration_roles.routing_basis: The paper cites this exact theorem as the summability control for the subsequent one-coordinate update calculation; the authored node records only the theorem's direct dominated-series content.
